name: bungee-pro-experiment
description: Hand-authored registry modeled from observations of bungee-pro.webflow.io. See variant-rationale.md for human judgments made.

components.name: Button
components.description: Primary CTA button. Two variants observed on bungee-pro: ghost (inline, no bg) and solid (filled dark).

components.name: ProjectCard
components.description: Project showcase card: full-bleed image with 32px rounded corners, logo overlay, info row with title + date below.

components.name: TestimonialCard
components.description: Testimonial card: light-gray bg, 32px radius, 2-column grid (image left, quote right).

bg.default.reason: GSS: bungee-pro declares --colors--white: white and applies it to body background. Direct mapping.

bg.muted.reason: GSS: AMBIGUOUS: chose bg.muted over border.muted because the hex appears as solid background on .testimonial-card and .footer (section-level treatment). However, it also appears as semi-transparent overlay (#eef0f64d) on .template-content-item, which is arguably a border-adjacent use. A style-signature pipeline without provenance would have to make this same call without the CSS context I had. Webflow's authors named this --colors--light-gray, avoiding either DCP role name entirely.

text.primary.reason: GSS: bungee-pro declares --colors--black: #1e1e1e and applies it as body { color: var(--colors--black) }. Direct mapping to DCP's text.primary.

text.muted.reason: GSS: bungee-pro declares --colors--text: #5a6271 and applies it to secondary text elements (project-card-date-block, template-content-item). Maps cleanly to text.muted.

text.disabled.reason: GSS: AMBIGUOUS: chose text.disabled but could arguably be a second text.muted tone. bungee-pro declares --colors--gray: #8a919b as a distinct role from --colors--text (#5a6271); DCP's contract has only one text.muted slot. A human picked text.disabled as the closest-fit residual role; an automated pipeline would either collapse #8a919b and #5a6271 into text.muted (losing the author's two-tone intent) or pick differently from DCP's roster. This is the role contract forcing a decision where the source vocabulary is richer than the target vocabulary.

border.default.reason: GSS: bungee-pro declares --colors--border: #d0d8e4 and uses it on border: 1px solid of .template-content-item. Direct mapping.

intent.danger.reason: GSS: Observed as a standalone red hex in the stylesheet, not assigned to a --colors--* custom property. Most likely source is a form validation error state (bungee-pro has newsletter form). Intent is inferred, not declared — a style-signature pipeline would capture this hex but not know whether to call it intent.danger or accent.warm.
